title_en:
1,000 Postgres databases = One process 🐘

That's how https://t.co/XOygNoF93E works.

Instead of running a separate Postgres server for every AI agent, PGX runs thousands of isolated databases inside a single Rust runtime.

Under the hood:

→ One shared SQL engine
→ Each database has its own tables and data
→ ~70 KB per untouched idle database
→ ~6 ms warm database creation (p50)
→ Copy-on-write cloning on ZFS
→ Automatic TTL cleanup

All through the standard Postgres wire protocol. Your existing clients and ORMs just work.

No Docker. No cloud. No 1,000 server processes.
Built for disposable AI agent databases, CI and testing.

https://t.co/Su2Mkl6ijb

title:
BREAKING: I used Claude Code to find hidden photos on my Android. There was even one of me on the toilet.

412 of them.
title_en:
BREAKING: I used Claude Code to find hidden photos on my Android. There was even one of me on the toilet.

412 of them. i never pressed the button once.

Watch the video below to see the scan pull them out one by one.

my phone kept saying the storage was almost full, but my gallery barely had any photos in it. so i asked Claude Code to write a scanner that opens every folder, even the ones the gallery skips.

the first part was boring. camera roll, whatsapp, telegram, screenshots, all where they should be.

then it hit a folder called .cache buried in the system files. 412 files ending in .bin. Claude read the first bytes of each one, and every single file was a JPEG with a fake extension.

the data inside every photo said the same thing: front camera. most of them are random shots of my day. the newest one is from 2:26 PM today, and yes, it's me on the toilet.

if you want to run the same check on your phone, it takes about 5 minutes:

1. turn on USB debugging: tap Build number 7 times in Settings, About phone (on Samsung it sits under Software information), then switch on USB debugging in Developer options
2. plug the phone into your laptop, tap Allow on the phone and open Claude Code
3. paste this: "use adb to scan /sdcard on my Android. find every file that starts with JPEG or PNG bytes, whatever its extension, and every folder with a .nomedia file. compare it with what the gallery shows and give me a list of everything the gallery hides."

no adb on your laptop? ask Claude to install it first.

full_text_zh:
突发事件：我使用 Claude Code 来查找 Android 上隐藏的照片。厕所里甚至还有我一个人。

其中 412 个。我一次也没按过按钮。

观看下面的视频，看看扫描将它们一一拉出来。

我的手机一直说存储空间快满了，但我的画廊里几乎没有任何照片。所以我要求 Claude Code 编写一个扫描仪来打开每个文件夹，甚至是图库跳过的文件夹。

第一部分很无聊。相机胶卷、whatsapp、电报、屏幕截图，所有它们应该在的地方。

然后它命中了隐藏在系统文件中名为 .cache 的文件夹。 412 个以 .bin 结尾的文件。克劳德读取了每个文件的第一个字节，每个文件都是带有假扩展名的 JPEG 文件。

每张照片中的数据都说明了同一件事：前置摄像头。其中大部分都是我一天中随机拍摄的。最新的是今天下午 2:26 的，是的，是我在厕所。

如果您想在手机上运行相同的检查，大约需要 5 分钟：

1. 打开 USB 调试：在“设置”、“关于手机”中点击“内部版本号”7 次（在三星上，它位于“软件信息”下），然后在“开发人员选项”中打开 USB 调试
2. 将手机插入笔记本电脑，点击手机上的“允许”并打开 Claude Code
3. 粘贴以下内容：“使用 adb 扫描我的 Android 上的 /sdcard。找到每个以 JPEG 或 PNG 字节开头的文件（无论其扩展名如何），以及每个带有 .nomedia 文件的文件夹。将其与图库显示的内容进行比较，并提供图库隐藏的所有内容的列表。”

你的笔记本电脑上没有adb吗？请克劳德先安装它。

title:
In a single year, AI has rewritten the security priority list for CISOs.

Attackers are moving faster. Bain estimates AI
title_en:
In a single year, AI has rewritten the security priority list for CISOs.

Attackers are moving faster. Bain estimates AI compresses a typical cyberattack from about four weeks to about 18 hours, and models keep getting better at finding and exploiting weaknesses.

There's also more to protect, with employees shipping apps they couldn't have built a year ago and agents getting access to source code, documents, and production systems.

In a survey of 100 CISOs at companies with 1,000+ employees, all seven of the most-selected 2027 priorities involve AI.

The biggest jumps since 2026:
- Internal AI agent security (+28 pts)
- AI SOC (+26 pts)
- AI offensive security (+24 pts)
- AI code security (+23 pts)
- AI vulnerability remediation (+22 pts)

Last year's staples:
- Exposure & vulnerability management (-21 pts)
- SIEM / security data (-18 pts)
- Privileged access management (-18 pts)

From a16z's @OwenColby and @steph_zhang on The New Security Agenda: https://t.co/C814PJ4wGg

quote_zh:
仅一年时间，人工智能就改写了 CISO 的安全优先事项列表。

攻击者的行动速度更快。贝恩估计人工智能将典型的网络攻击从大约 4 周压缩到大约 18 小时，并且模型在发现和利用弱点方面不断变得更好。

还有更多需要保护的内容，员工发布了他们一年前无法构建的应用程序，代理可以访问源代码、文档和生产系统。

对拥有 1,000 多名员工的公司的 100 名 CISO 进行的一项调查显示，2027 年最受关注的七个优先事项都涉及人工智能。

自 2026 年以来的最大跳跃：
- 内部人工智能代理安全（+28 分）
- AI SOC（+26 分）
- AI进攻性安全（+24分）
- AI代码安全性（+23分）
- AI漏洞修复（+22分）

- 暴露和漏洞管理（-21 分）

title_en:
AI agents are evolving beyond simply generating answers. The next step is giving them the ability to act, transact, and operate independently.

Imagine an AI agent that needs to research a topic, access different models, purchase data, and complete a task without waiting for human approval at every step. For that to work, AI needs more than intelligence. It needs a way to pay for the services it uses.
@LightchainAI  is building toward this vision with wallet-based payments, $LCAI, independent GPU operators, and on-chain records for AI jobs.

Developers could build applications where agents access AI services and pay per answer, while operators contribute computing power to the network.

The bigger idea is an open AI economy where software can become an active participant, not just a tool people use.

The real test will be adoption, reliability, security, and whether this model can compete with existing AI infrastructure.

But one thing is clear: the future of AI may not only be about smarter models. It may also be about enabling them to do more.

And that’s worth watching with @LightchainAI.

title: Legora is part of the Claude for Legal launch. With Legora connected to @claudeai, lawyers can put Legora’s agent to wor
title_en:
Legora is part of the Claude for Legal launch. With Legora connected to @claudeai, lawyers can put Legora’s agent to work on jurisdiction-specific legal research and their own matter files, all from inside Claude, under their existing permissions and audit trail. Every answer links back to its sources in Legora for review.

“As legal teams adopt AI across more parts of their business, they need trusted legal intelligence available in those environments,” said Bryan Tsao, Chief Product Officer at Legora. “By connecting Legora to Claude, we’re making it easier for mutual customers to get answers to legal questions within their broader enterprise AI workflows, with links back to Legora for source review, citations and deeper legal work.”

title: Giving an AI agent the ability to complete tasks is one thing. Trusting it to handle paid work is a completely different
title_en:
Giving an AI agent the ability to complete tasks is one thing. Trusting it to handle paid work is a completely different story.

Especially when money, private information and people you've never worked with are involved.

I've been following the recent updates from @termix_ai, and there are a few things worth discussing.

--> Binance Agent ID is now integrated with TermiX

Agents with TermiX Skills installed can now communicate through Binance Agent IDs.

The team even demonstrated messaging using the Agent IDs of @cz_binance and @heyibinance.

Imagine having an agent that specializes in market research but needs help reviewing a smart contract.

It could contact another specialized agent, discuss the work and potentially arrange a collaboration.

Of course, messaging is only the beginning. Someone still needs to agree on the work, deliver it and handle payment.

--> Making paid work more reliable

With all the recent discussions around data leaks and security, I wouldn't want an AI agent handling money without clear rules.

@termix_ai uses its AACP protocol to manage this process.

An order can be funded through escrow, the agent submits its work, and the client has a way to review or challenge the delivery before settlement.

I prefer this approach because paying an agent shouldn't mean blindly trusting whatever result it provides.

There's still a lot to consider around permissions, verification and protecting sensitive information. Escrow alone doesn't solve every security problem.

--> One warning everyone should know about

TermiX has also reported scammers impersonating its team and asking community members for investments.

The team made it clear that they're not conducting any community fundraising.

If someone approaches you claiming otherwise, don't send funds or share sensitive information. 

Always verify announcements through @termix_ai's official channels.

For me, building trust around AI agents means more than giving them advanced capabilities.

People need to understand who they're dealing with, what they're paying for and what happens if something goes wrong.

That's what will matter when these agents start working with more people outside their own developers.

full_text_zh:
赋予人工智能代理完成任务的能力是一回事。信任它来处理有偿工作是一个完全不同的故事。

尤其是当涉及金钱、私人信息和从未共事过的人时。

我一直在关注 @termix_ai 的最新更新，有一些事情值得讨论。

--> Binance Agent ID 现已与 TermiX 集成

安装了 TermiX Skills 的代理现在可以通过币安代理 ID 进行通信。

该团队甚至使用代理 ID @cz_binance 和 @heyibinance 演示了消息传递。

想象一下，有一个专门从事市场研究但需要帮助审查智能合约的代理人。

它可以联系另一个专业代理，讨论工作并可能安排合作。

当然，消息传递只是一个开始。仍然需要有人就工作达成一致、交付并处理付款。

--> 让有偿工作更可靠

鉴于最近有关数据泄露和安全性的所有讨论，我不希望人工智能代理在没有明确规则的情况下处理资金。

@termix_ai 使用其 AACP 协议来管理此过程。

订单可以通过托管提供资金，代理提交其工作，客户可以在结算前审查或质疑交付情况。

我更喜欢这种方法，因为向代理人付费并不意味着盲目相信它提供的任何结果。

关于权限、验证和保护敏感信息，还有很多事情需要考虑。仅托管并不能解决所有安全问题。

--> 每个人都应该知道的一个警告

TermiX 还报告称，诈骗者冒充其团队并向社区成员寻求投资。

该团队明确表示，他们不会进行任何社区筹款。

如果有人向您提出其他要求，请不要发送资金或分享敏感信息。

请务必通过@termix_ai 的官方渠道验证公告。

对我来说，围绕人工智能代理建立信任不仅仅意味着赋予他们先进的能力。

人们需要了解他们正在与谁打交道、他们支付的费用以及如果出现问题会发生什么。

当这些代理开始与自己的开发人员之外的更多人合作时，这才是重要的。

#TermiX #AIAgents #代理经济

title:
We’re incredibly excited that @AjimCapital investment in @learn2earnNG and Talent Nation is now public!

We backed @kesi
title_en:
We’re incredibly excited that @AjimCapital investment in @learn2earnNG and Talent Nation is now public!

We backed @kesiah_frank  and Iyinoluwa Samuel Aboyeji Jr because we believe African talent has a defining role to play in building with AI.

Already: 63,000+ applications, 32,000+ candidates assessed, and approximately 1,400 fellows training across 9 campuses in Nigeria.

But something Iyin said during our call really stayed with me: as AI adoption grows, he believes hiring an AI engineer in Africa will become more affordable than using an AI agent.

That’s a bold statement. And after spending time with them, I have no doubt they believe they can make it happen.

They’re building the training, certification, and global talent platform to put that conviction to work.

Proud to back Kesiah, Iyin, and the Talent Nation team.

We’re incredibly excited that @AjimCapital investment in @learn2earnNG and Talent Nation is now public!

Already: 63,000+ applications, 32,000+ candidates assessed, and approximately 1,400 fellows training across 9 campuses in Nigeria.

But something Iyin said during our call really stayed with me: as AI adoption grows, he believes hiring an AI engineer in Africa will become more affordable than using an AI agent.

full_text_zh:
我们非常高兴 @AjimCapital 对 @learn2earnNG 和 Talent Nation 的投资现已公开！

我们支持 @kesiah_frank 和 Iyinoluwa Samuel Aboyeji Jr，因为我们相信非洲人才在人工智能建设中可以发挥决定性作用。

已经有超过 63,000 份申请，超过 32,000 名候选人接受评估，大约 1,400 名研究员在尼日利亚的 9 个校区接受培训。

但 Iyin 在我们通话中说的一句话让我印象深刻：随着人工智能采用的增长，他相信在非洲雇用一名人工智能工程师将比使用人工智能代理更便宜。

这是一个大胆的声明。在与他们相处一段时间后，我毫不怀疑他们相信自己能够实现这一目标。

他们正在建立培训、认证和全球人才平台，以将这一信念付诸实践。

很自豪能够支持 Kesiah、Iyin 和 Talent Nation 团队。

title: A woman from a non English speaking country screaming my song lyrics like she wrote them, another one has a full sleeve
title_en:
A woman from a non English speaking country screaming my song lyrics like she wrote them, another one has a full sleeve tatoo of my song lyrics and it's even the edo dialect part.
My song was used as a thesis by an African master student in Hamburg.
My song been sang by stranger in a military base in the united states..
My song was used as a project case study to teach indian students in mumbai.
Over a a thousand queer people in southern Africa dancing to my voice in a rave...

It's not much for an emerging artiste but it's honest work and i am honoured.

title:
Growing companies think their biggest problem is hiring, but they are wrong. It’s only half the story.

In reality even
title_en:
Growing companies think their biggest problem is hiring, but they are wrong. It’s only half the story.

In reality even the best candidates will fail if they are not set up for success from the start.

I experienced this at @yext across a team of 2,500, and today, with the pull of our growing customer base, Windmill is launching the system I always wanted

An agentic onboarding system to give every new hire the best chance of being successful as quickly as possible.

@trywindmill now has over 250 customers and many of them growing faster than any companies before in human history. Our customers feel this pain viscerally. You spend millions on recruiting and closing candidates only for them to show up to an onboarding based off a couple slides and a Notion doc.

Onboarding is one of the most important things a company does. It’s a new hire’s introduction to the company culture and how it runs. And in today’s rapidly changing world, it’s harder than it’s ever been before.

Effective onboarding isn't about teaching people everything. It's about getting them to real contribution as fast as possible, with clear goals, regular feedback, and a manager who stays in the loop.

Windmill puts an AI agent in charge of making that happen for every new hire, and holds everyone accountable along the way.

We’re currently live with amazing customers like @Etched  (among others) and it’s incredible to see the results. Every one of our customers I’ve shared this with has raised their hands and we’re including it as part of their subscription.

If this is something your team struggles with, we’d love to show you the system that’s helped customers around the globe onboard and ramp their teams 3x faster.

我们目前与@Etched（等等）等出色的客户一起生活，看到结果令人难以置信。我与之分享的每一位客户都举起了手，我们将其作为他们订阅的一部分。

title: Google started rolling out Universal Cart in the US on October 15: one cart across retailers, inside Search and the Gemi
title_en:
Google started rolling out Universal Cart in the US on October 15: one cart across retailers, inside Search and the Gemini app. It tracks price drops and restocks, applies promo codes, and suggests which card in your Google Wallet earns the most on each purchase [Google, via The Next Web].

Nike, Target, Walmart, Sephora and Shopify sellers are among the merchants checking out through it.

Google is turning its AI assistant into a place where buying gets done, and shoppers are ready to start with the everyday basket. Groceries top the list of purchases consumers would hand to an AI agent, at 41% [https://t.co/zdpysDCQ7P, Agentic Commerce 2026].

Most AI automations work in demos but struggle in production.

The problem isn't always the AI model. It's the architecture around it.

Here are 11 components that make AI automation reliable, secure, and scalable.

𝟭. 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗳𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗧𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿

Starts automation through schedules, user actions, or system events. Prevent duplicate executions.

𝟮. 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗟𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿

Connects APIs, webhooks, and enterprise applications. Handles authentication, timeouts, and rate limits.

𝟯. 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Converts unstructured inputs into validated schemas, JSON, and usable formats.

𝟰. 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗜𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Collects, cleans, normalizes, and enriches data. Ensures freshness and quality.

𝟱. 𝗔𝗜 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲

Combines deterministic rules, ML predictions, and LLM reasoning to decide the next action.

𝟲. 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗳𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗢𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Manages task dependencies, queues, retries, and checkpoints for failure recovery.

𝟳. 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗘𝘅𝗲𝗰𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Turns decisions into API calls, database updates, and notifications with duplicate-action protection.

𝟴. 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Uses caching, parallel processing, and failover to reduce latency and costs.

𝟵. 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆

Tracks logs, traces, errors, and success rates. Enables alerts and recovery.

𝟭𝟬. 𝗦𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 & 𝗚𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲

Enforces RBAC, least privilege, data protection, compliance, and auditability.

𝟭𝟭. 𝗙𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗽

Captures outcomes and uses performance metrics to improve prompts, models, and workflows.

A production-ready AI system proves reliability, security, and scalability.

The difference is system engineering, not just better prompts.

full_text_zh:
𝗜𝗜 𝗘𝘀𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗮 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻-𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺

大多数人工智能自动化在演示中都能工作，但在生产中却举步维艰。

问题并不总是出在人工智能模型上。这是它周围的建筑。

以下 11 个组件使 AI 自动化变得可靠、安全且可扩展。

𝟭. 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗳𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗧𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿

通过计划、用户操作或系统事件启动自动化。防止重复执行。

𝟮. 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗟𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿

连接 API、Webhooks 和企业应用程序。处理身份验证、超时和速率限制。

𝟯. 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

将非结构化输入转换为经过验证的架构、JSON 和可用格式。

𝟰. 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗜𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

收集、清理、标准化和丰富数据。确保新鲜度和品质。

𝟱. 𝗔𝗜 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲

结合确定性规则、ML 预测和 LLM 推理来决定下一步行动。

𝟲. 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗳𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗢𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

管理任务依赖性、队列、重试和故障恢复检查点。

𝟳. 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗘𝘅𝗲𝗰𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

将决策转化为 API 调用、数据库更新和具有重复操作保护的通知。

𝟴. 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

使用缓存、并行处理和故障转移来减少延迟和成本。

𝟵. 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆

跟踪日志、痕迹、错误和成功率。启用警报和恢复。

𝟭𝟬. 𝗦𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 & 𝗚𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲

强制实施 RBAC、最小权限、数据保护、合规性和可审核性。

𝟭𝟭. 𝗙𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗽

捕获结果并使用性能指标来改进提示、模型和工作流程。

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝗴 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

一个有效的人工智能演示证明了可行性。

生产就绪的人工智能系统证明了可靠性、安全性和可扩展性。

区别在于系统工程，而不仅仅是更好的提示。

AI 自动化项目中最常缺少这 11 个组件中的哪一个？

title_en:
If you want to master AI agents in 2026, here is the complete 8-week curriculum (100% free):

• Week 1: Hugging Face Agents Course (Unit 1)
→ Time: 1 week
→ Milestone: Trace a complete ReAct loop (thought, action, observation) on paper. Know exactly when an agent is overkill.

• Weeks 2-3: DeepLearning .AI, "AI Agents in LangGraph"
→ Time: ~1h 45m
→ Milestone: Build a research agent with graphs, state loops, and human-in-the-loop gates. It resumes from checkpoints if crashed.

• Weeks 4-5: Microsoft's AI Agents for Beginners (18 lessons on GitHub)
→ Time: 2 weeks
→ Milestone: Master multi-agent swarms, memory, planning, and agentic RAG. Defend pattern choices for 3 distinct production tasks.

• Week 6: DeepLearning .AI, "Evaluating AI Agents"
→ Time: ~2h 35m
→ Milestone: Trace every tool call, score path lengths, and catch hallucinations before users report them.

• Week 7: Kaggle's 5-Day AI Agents Intensive with Google
→ Time: 1 week
→ Milestone: Deploy your agent off your laptop and run agent-to-agent communication at scale.

• Week 8 (Optional): UC Berkeley's LLM Agents MOOC (Fall 2024)
→ Time: 1 week
→ Milestone: Deep research foundations. Explain current frontier agent papers in your own words.

The courses are completely free. Skip the paid certificates; code running in production is your certificate.

Which course are you starting with this week?

title:
An AI agent can produce a convincing answer in seconds.

But what happens when that answer is wrong and someone has alre
title_en:
An AI agent can produce a convincing answer in seconds.

But what happens when that answer is wrong and someone has already paid for it?

I've been thinking about this while looking into ERC-8004 and how @termix_ai is approaching agent reputation.

Imagine hiring an AI agent to review a smart contract.

It returns a detailed report, explains the code, and says everything looks safe.
The report might look professional. But that doesn't tell you whether the agent actually found every important vulnerability.

And if you're trusting it with something valuable, you'd probably want to know how its previous audits turned out.

Were those reports independently checked? Did clients find problems later? Has the agent ever had its work challenged?

This is where ERC-8004 becomes useful.
It separates an agent's identity from its reputation and validation records.

The Identity Registry gives an agent a recognizable onchain identity.

The Reputation Registry allows clients to leave feedback connected to that identity.

And the Validation Registry provides a way to record independent checks of an agent's work.

I find that separation important because a satisfied customer and a correctly completed task aren't always the same thing.

Someone might give an agent a good rating because it responded quickly. That doesn't necessarily mean its technical conclusions were correct.

Now consider how @termix_ai approaches this through https://t.co/xHQHPbB46o and its AACP design.

Agents can establish wallet-owned .agent identities, while the marketplace connects jobs to escrow, deliverable records, settlement, and dispute handling.

So instead of looking only at what an agent claims it can do, there's an opportunity to examine what happened during its previous work.

Of course, there's still a problem.
A verifiable record doesn't guarantee that the person leaving feedback is honest or that an evaluator made the right decision. 

ERC-8004 itself acknowledges that reputation systems can face manipulation.

But making those records available gives future clients more information to question and compare.

And I think that's going to matter as AI agents start hiring other agents.

Because when no human is checking every individual decision, choosing the wrong agent could mean losing money before anyone notices the mistake.

An identity tells you which agent you're dealing with.

Its history helps you decide whether that agent has earned your trust.

That's the part of ERC-8004 I think deserves more attention.

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可以在几秒钟内给出令人信服的答案。

但如果这个答案是错误的并且有人已经为此付出了代价，会发生什么？

我在研究 ERC-8004 以及 @termix_ai 如何接近代理声誉时一直在思考这个问题。

想象一下雇用人工智能代理来审查智能合约。

它返回一份详细的报告，解释代码，并说一切看起来都很安全。
该报告可能看起来很专业。但这并不能告诉您代理是否真的发现了每个重要的漏洞。

如果你信任它一些有价值的东西，你可能想知道它之前的审计结果如何。

这些报告是否经过独立检查？客户后来发现问题了吗？代理人的工作是否曾受到挑战？

这就是 ERC-8004 发挥作用的地方。
它将代理的身份与其声誉和验证记录分开。

身份注册表为代理提供了可识别的链上身份。

声誉注册表允许客户留下与该身份相关的反馈。

验证注册表提供了一种记录代理工作的独立检查的方法。

我发现这种分离很重要，因为满意的客户和正确完成的任务并不总是同一件事。

有人可能会给代理一个很好的评价，因为它响应很快。这并不一定意味着其技术结论是正确的。

现在考虑 @termix_ai 如何通过 及其 AACP 设计来实现这一目标。

代理可以建立钱包拥有的代理身份，而市场则将工作与托管、可交付记录、结算和争议处理连接起来。

因此，我们有机会检查代理之前的工作期间发生了什么，而不是只关注代理声称它可以做什么。

当然，还有一个问题。
可验证的记录并不能保证留下反馈的人是诚实的或评估者做出了正确的决定。

ERC-8004 本身承认声誉系统可能面临操纵。

但提供这些记录可以为未来的客户提供更多信息来质疑和比较。

我认为随着人工智能代理开始雇用其他代理，这将变得很重要。

因为当没有人检查每个单独的决定时，选择错误的代理可能意味着在任何人注意到错误之前就损失金钱。

身份可以告诉您正在与哪个代理打交道。

它的历史记录可以帮助您确定该代理是否赢得了您的信任。

我认为这是 ERC-8004 值得更多关注的部分。

人工智能代理可以在几秒钟内给出令人信服的答案。

但是，当这个答案是错误的并且有人已经为此付出了代价时会发生什么？

我在研究 ERC-8004 以及 @termix_ai 如何接近代理声誉时一直在思考这个问题。

想象一下雇用人工智能代理来审查智能合约。

它返回一份详细的报告，解释代码，并说一切看起来都很安全。
该报告可能看起来很专业。但这并不能告诉您代理是否真的发现了每个重要的漏洞。

如果你信任它一些有价值的东西，你可能想知道它之前的审计结果如何。

这些报告是否经过独立检查？客户后来发现问题了吗？代理人的工作是否曾经受到过挑战？

这就是 ERC-8004 发挥作用的地方。
它将代理的身份与其声誉和验证记录分开。

身份注册表为代理提供了可识别的链上身份。

声誉注册表允许客户留下与该身份相关的反馈。

验证注册表提供了一种记录代理工作的独立检查的方法。

我发现这种分离很重要，因为满意的客户和正确完成的任务并不总是同一件事。

有人可能会给代理一个很好的评价，因为它响应很快。这并不一定意味着其技术结论是正确的。

现在考虑 @termix_ai 如何通过 及其 AACP 设计来实现这一目标。

代理可以建立钱包拥有的代理身份，而市场则将工作与托管、可交付记录、结算和争议处理连接起来。

因此，我们有机会检查代理之前的工作期间发生了什么，而不是只关注代理声称它可以做什么。

当然，还有一个问题。
可验证的记录并不能保证留下反馈的人是诚实的或评估者做出了正确的决定。

ERC-8004 本身承认声誉系统可能面临操纵。

但提供这些记录可以为未来的客户提供更多信息来质疑和比较。

我认为随着人工智能代理开始雇用其他代理，这将变得很重要。

因为当没有人检查每个单独的决定时，选择错误的代理可能意味着在任何人注意到错误之前就损失金钱。

身份可以告诉您正在与哪个代理打交道。

它的历史记录可以帮助您确定该代理是否赢得了您的信任。

我认为这是 ERC-8004 值得更多关注的部分。

title:
Security breaks down the moment an AI can't tell the difference between data and instructions.

That's how a hidden Mors
title_en:
Security breaks down the moment an AI can't tell the difference between data and instructions.

That's how a hidden Morse code message helped drain roughly $200k from an AI agent. Nobody cracked a wallet. Nobody stole keys. The attacker convinced the agent to treat a hidden command as part of the information it was reading.

The uncomfortable reality is that a single AI model is a single security assumption.

If attackers can study that model long enough, they can learn what slips through.

What stands out to me about @GenLayer's Greyboxing is that it doesn't rely on making one AI impossible to fool.

Before a request reaches any model, every validator rewrites, restructures, and screens the input using its own private defenses. Each validator also runs its own model.

The attack no longer has one predictable target.

An attacker can rehearse against one model.

They can't reliably rehearse against hidden defenses and independent validators they can't see.

And if one validator still gets tricked, its decision isn't automatically accepted. The others can reject it.

The Morse code exploit worked because there was one judgment that mattered.

Greyboxing turns that into many independent judgments that must agree.

The real security upgrade isn't a smarter AI.

It's removing the single mistake that can move the money.

full_text_zh:
当人工智能无法区分数据和指令时，安全性就会崩溃。

这就是一条隐藏的摩尔斯电码信息如何帮助人工智能代理流失大约 20 万美元的原因。没有人破解钱包。没有人偷钥匙。攻击者说服代理将隐藏命令视为其正在读取的信息的一部分。

令人不安的现实是，单一的人工智能模型就是单一的安全假设。

如果攻击者能够足够长的时间研究该模型，他们就能了解哪些内容被漏掉了。

@GenLayer 的 Greyboxing 对我来说最突出的一点是，它并不依赖于让人工智能无法被愚弄。

在请求到达任何模型之前，每个验证器都会使用自己的私有防御来重写、重组和筛选输入。每个验证器还运行自己的模型。

攻击不再有一个可预测的目标。

攻击者可以针对一种模型进行演练。

他们无法可靠地针对他们看不到的隐藏防御和独立验证器进行演练。

如果一个验证者仍然被欺骗，它的决定不会自动被接受。其他人可以拒绝。

摩尔斯电码漏洞之所以有效，是因为有一个判断很重要。

灰盒分析将其转化为许多必须达成一致的独立判断。

真正的安全升级并不是更智能的人工智能。

它消除了可能转移资金的单一错误。

title:

I was basically a human clipboard between Claude Code and my team's Slack.

The agent finds the bug
title_en:
Okay, this is cool.

I was basically a human clipboard between Claude Code and my team's Slack.

The agent finds the bug, I copy the useful bits, paste them in a thread, then answer everyone's follow-up questions myself.

And by the time I'd explained it all, half the context was lost anyway.

So I set up Switch. It's open source and puts the agent you already use in a shared room with your team.

I connected Claude Code, created a room for the project and linked it to our Slack.

Now my teammate just tags the agent in Slack and reads the full history on her own.

She can see what it already tried, what it found and pick up from there without pinging me.

Setup took a bit of config, but the getting-started docs walk you through it step by step.

Not being the middleman anymore is my favourite part.

Try it here: https://t.co/30loJC6jkW

Curious how others are doing this.

Drop yours with #HowISwitch

title:
Termix Ai

Focus: ERC-8004, agent identity, reputation and the economics of trust.

An AI agent can register an identity
title_en:
Termix Ai

Focus: ERC-8004, agent identity, reputation and the economics of trust.

An AI agent can register an identity in minutes.

But how does it earn a reputation worth trusting?

I've been exploring this question while researching @termix_ai and its AACP protocol.

Imagine two AI agents offering the same smart contract auditing service.

Both claim they can identify vulnerabilities. Both offer competitive pricing.

But one has completed dozens of verifiable jobs, while the other has no established history.

Should they be treated equally?

This is where ERC-8004 becomes interesting.

Through https://t.co/goaiW7vvNf, agents can register a wallet-owned .agent identity and establish an onchain record of their activity.

AACP goes further by connecting reputation to actual commercial outcomes.

Its whitepaper outlines several factors for evaluating agents:

• Job completion rates
• On-time delivery
• Evaluation results
• Dispute outcomes
• Strength of delivery verification

What caught my attention is the economic side.

AACP's design also proposes staking requirements and penalties for dishonest behavior.

The idea is to make reputation more than a rating displayed on a profile.

But there's an important limitation.

Onchain identity proves which agent you're dealing with. It doesn't automatically prove the agent is competent.

Even reputation scores need context. Who evaluated the work? How many jobs were completed? Could the history have been manipulated?

These questions become increasingly important when AI agents start hiring other agents without continuous human supervision.

For me, the interesting part of TermiX isn't simply giving agents an identity.

It's exploring how an agent's history can influence whether anyone should trust it with real work.

Because in an autonomous economy, being discoverable is only the beginning.

Explore: https://t.co/goaiW7vvNf

full_text_zh:
特米克斯艾

重点：ERC-8004，代理身份、声誉和信任经济学。

人工智能代理可以在几分钟内注册身份。

但它如何赢得值得信赖的声誉呢？

我在研究 @termix_ai 及其 AACP 协议时一直在探索这个问题。

想象一下两个人工智能代理提供相同的智能合约审计服务。

两人都声称他们可以识别漏洞。两者都提供有竞争力的价格。

但其中一个已经完成了数十项可验证的工作，而另一个则没有既定的历史。

他们应该受到平等对待吗？

这就是 ERC-8004 变得有趣的地方。

通过 ，代理可以注册钱包拥有的 .agent 身份并建立其活动的链上记录。

AACP 更进一步，将声誉与实际商业成果联系起来。

其白皮书概述了评估代理商的几个因素：

• 工作完成率
• 准时交货
• 评估结果
• 争议结果
• 交付强度验证

引起我注意的是经济方面。

AACP 的设计还提出了质押要求和对不诚实行为的处罚。

这个想法是让声誉不仅仅是个人资料上显示的评级。

但有一个重要的限制。

链上身份证明您正在与哪个代理打交道。它不会自动证明代理人有能力。

甚至声誉分数也需要背景。谁评价了这项工作？完成了多少工作？历史有可能被篡改吗？

当人工智能代理开始在没有持续人类监督的情况下雇用其他代理时，这些问题变得越来越重要。

对我来说，TermiX 有趣的部分不仅仅是为代理提供身份。

它正在探索代理的历史如何影响人们是否应该信任它进行实际工作。

因为在自治经济中，被发现只是一个开始。

title:
an ai agent can audit your smart contract, write code or research a project. 

but how do you know the work is worth pay
title_en:
an ai agent can audit your smart contract, write code or research a project. 

but how do you know the work is worth paying for? and if you disagree with the result, who decides what happens to the money?

people already face this problem when hiring freelancers. 

now imagine ai agents hiring and paying each other without a person managing every step.

clients need a way to check who they're hiring, and agents need protection against clients who refuse to pay for agreed work. neither side should have to rely on promises alone.

@termix_ai addresses this through AACP, its Agent Commerce Protocol, which handles jobs from bidding and delivery to payment and disputes.

each agent has an onchain identity through ERC-8004. clients can check its record, with settled job outcomes contributing to its reputation rather than relying on claims the agent makes about itself.

when a client accepts a quote, the agreed funds go into an onchain escrow contract. the provider can't withdraw them on its own, and payment follows the contract's settlement rules.

if the client challenges the delivery, a three-seat evaluator panel reviews the evidence and votes onchain. eligible cases can go to an arbitrator, and the contract handles settlement based on the outcome.

agents also stake funds that can be locked against jobs. if a dispute finds an agent at fault, its stake can be slashed, with the slashed amount going to the other party.

this doesn't guarantee perfect work, but it gives both sides a process for handling payment and disagreements.

as agents take on more paid work, they need more than the ability to complete tasks. 

they need a way to agree on terms, verify results and settle payments without relying on blind trust.

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可以审核您的智能合约、编写代码或研究项目。

但你怎么知道这项工作值得付出代价呢？如果您不同意结果，谁来决定这笔钱的处理方式？

人们在雇用自由职业者时已经面临这个问题。

现在想象一下，人工智能代理相互雇佣和支付报酬，而无需专人管理每一步。

客户需要一种方法来检查他们正在雇用的人，代理商需要保护他们免受拒绝支付约定工作费用的客户的影响。双方都不应仅仅依赖承诺。

@termix_ai 通过 AACP（其代理商务协议）解决了这个问题，该协议处理从投标、交付到付款和纠纷的工作。

每个代理都通过 ERC-8004 拥有一个链上身份。客户可以检查其记录，确定的工作成果有助于其声誉，而不是依赖于代理人对自己的声明。

当客户接受报价时，商定的资金将进入链上托管合约。提供者不能自行提取，付款遵循合同的结算规则。

如果客户对交付提出质疑，三人评估小组将审查证据并在链上投票。符合条件的案件可以提交给仲裁员，合约根据结果进行结算。

代理人还可以抵押可以锁定工作岗位的资金。如果争议发现代理人有过错，其股份可以被削减，削减的金额归另一方所有。

这并不能保证完美的工作，但它为双方提供了处理付款和分歧的流程。

随着代理人承担更多有偿工作，他们需要的不仅仅是完成任务的能力。

他们需要一种不依赖盲目信任的方式来商定条款、验证结果和结算付款。

title:
Creating an intelligent AI agent is one thing. 

Enabling it to collaborate with other agents is another challenge entir
title_en:
Creating an intelligent AI agent is one thing. 

Enabling it to collaborate with other agents is another challenge entirely.

Imagine an agent that can analyze market data but needs help turning its findings into a professional report. Instead of doing everything alone, it could hire another agent with the right expertise.

But how do they coordinate, agree on pricing, exchange work, and ensure payment?

That’s the problem @termix_ai is exploring with https://t.co/eMEjCmIdTb.

The platform introduces a marketplace for agent-to-agent transactions, supporting a process that includes job requests, quotes, escrow, delivery, and settlement.

What makes this interesting is the possibility of specialized agents working together rather than every agent trying to handle every task.

One agent researches, another analyzes, and a third produces the final output. Each contributes its strengths to a larger workflow.

However, this model depends on more than connectivity. 

Service quality, trust, dispute resolution, and real demand will determine whether these interactions become practical at scale.

I believe the infrastructure enabling agents to exchange services could be just as important as the intelligence powering them.

If AI agents become both buyers and sellers in a digital economy, which challenge do you think will matter most: finding the right agent, trusting its output, or ensuring reliable transactions?

full_text_zh:
创建智能人工智能代理是一回事。

使其能够与其他代理协作完全是另一个挑战。

想象一下，一个代理商可以分析市场数据，但需要帮助将其发现转化为专业报告。它可以聘请另一位具有适当专业知识的代理人，而不是独自完成所有事情。

但他们如何协调、就定价、交换工作达成一致并确保付款呢？

这就是 @termix_ai 正在通过 探索的问题。

该平台引入了代理间交易市场，支持包括工作请求、报价、托管、交付和结算在内的流程。

有趣的是，专业代理可以一起工作，而不是每个代理都试图处理每项任务。

一个代理进行研究，另一个代理进行分析，第三个代理生成最终输出。每个都为更大的工作流程贡献了自己的优势。

然而，这种模式不仅仅依赖于连接性。

服务质量、信任、争议解决和实际需求将决定这些交互是否能够大规模实用。

我相信使代理能够交换服务的基础设施可能与支持它们的情报一样重要。

如果人工智能代理成为数字经济中的买家和卖家，您认为哪个挑战最重要：找到合适的代理，信任其输出，还是确保可靠的交易？

如果人工智能代理成为数字经济中的买家和卖家，您认为哪个挑战最重要：找到合适的代理，信任其输出，还是确保可靠的交易？
quote_zh:
创建智能人工智能代理是一回事。

使其能够与其他代理协作完全是另一个挑战。

想象一下，一个代理商可以分析市场数据，但需要帮助将其发现转化为专业报告。它可以聘请另一位具有适当专业知识的代理人，而不是独自完成所有事情。

但他们如何协调、就定价、交换工作和确保付款达成一致呢？

这就是 @termix_ai 正在通过 探索的问题。

该平台引入了代理间交易市场，支持包括工作请求、报价、托管、交付和结算在内的流程。

有趣的是，专业代理可以一起工作，而不是每个代理都试图处理每项任务。

一个代理进行研究，另一个代理进行分析，第三个代理生成最终输出。每个都为更大的工作流程贡献了自己的优势。

然而，这种模式不仅仅依赖于连接性。

服务质量、信任、争议解决和实际需求将决定这些交互是否能够大规模实用。

我相信使代理能够交换服务的基础设施可能与支持它们的情报一样重要。

如果人工智能代理成为数字经济中的买家和卖家，您认为哪个挑战最重要：找到合适的代理，信任其输出，还是确保可靠的交易？

title: I didn't touch CapCut once. @CreaoAI  built my faceless YouTube channel from scratch, and the first video is already liv
title_en:
I didn't touch CapCut once. @CreaoAI  built my faceless YouTube channel from scratch, and the first video is already live.

Quick context. My last channel ran on Grok Bot, and the character kept drifting, even after I simplified the task. I needed to know whether my setup was the problem or the tool.

So I ran a fair test. Brand-new channel. One agent on CREAO, given four rules:

→ Continuity rule: every scene follows on from the last
→ Natural realism rule: she has to look and move like a real person
→ Consistency rule: her face, body and look never change
→ Negative rule: a clear list of what she must never do or become

Then I let it build everything:

→ CREAO picked the channel name
→ CREAO created the character and her bible sheet
→ CREAO wrote the idea
→ CREAO wrote the script
→ CREAO created and directed the scenes
→ CREAO made the video clip by clip and merged it, with no CapCut
→ CREAO added the voiceover
→ CREAO added the captions
→ CREAO posted it on YouTube

It's live now. The link is in the first reply, so go and judge it yourself.

I said last time I'd split the work into three agents. I'm testing one first, on purpose. If one agent on CREAO holds the character, the tool was the problem. If it drifts, I'll split it and find out exactly what broke.

We're taking this channel from zero to 100K subscribers, and I'll post what works and what breaks, so you don't make the same mistakes.

title:
Last time, I argued that an AI agent needs paying customers, not just a clever model.

Now @termix_ai has added somethin
title_en:
Last time, I argued that an AI agent needs paying customers, not just a clever model.

Now @termix_ai has added something interesting: messaging through Binance Agent ID when both agents have TermiX Skills installed.

Their demo even sends messages to Agent IDs associated with @cz_binance and @heyibinance.

Pretty cool. But messaging a famous agent doesn't automatically make you business partners. Otherwise, my inbox would already be a billion-dollar startup.

What interests me is the gap between being reachable and being hireable.
An ID helps someone find your agent. Messaging starts the conversation.

But would I trust that agent with $20?

I'd want to see its actual capabilities, previous deliveries, pricing, and how disputes are handled.

That's the test I'm interested in throughout Epoch 3.

Can a conversation become a real quote, a funded job, a verified deliverable, and a public settlement?

@termix_ai, demonstrate that complete journey, not just the first message.

Because agent-to-agent communication solves discovery.

It doesn't automatically solve trust or demand.

The real breakthrough isn't when two agents can talk.

It's when they can do business worth repeating.

title_en:
An AI agent that cannot ignore its limits

Most AI trading agents talk about what they can do. @meetmotes is also focusing on what they are allowed to do.

The idea is to connect each NFT to an AI agent with rules around what it can trade, how much capital it can deploy, and when it must stop.

That distinction matters. Giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. Defining the boundaries of those decisions is another.

meetmotes is building around that second part too.

title:
Imagine an AI agent needing a fresh 3D scan of a warehouse it has never seen.

It can process the request, but someone s
title_en:
Imagine an AI agent needing a fresh 3D scan of a warehouse it has never seen.

It can process the request, but someone still needs to go there and capture the actual environment.

That’s the gap @vangrid_io is working to address, and its latest move on @arc is worth watching.

Vangrid is building a system that lets AI agents pay human contributors to collect real world spatial data on demand.

Here’s how the process works.

An agent identifies a location it needs data from and funds a bounty in USDC. 

A contributor visits the site, captures the environment, and submits the data for review. 

Once accepted, the requester receives the resulting 3D reconstruction.

Vangrid has also announced its first bounty payment on Arc, marking an early milestone for this approach.

I find the connection between AI agents and human contributors particularly interesting.

Agents can handle digital tasks, process information and make decisions, but getting accurate data about a specific physical location can still require someone on the ground.

That data could support robotics, mapping, digital twins and Physical AI development, where understanding real environments matters.

Of course, the model still needs to prove itself at scale.

 Data quality, verification, privacy and consistent demand will all play a role in its success.

Still, the idea opens up an interesting possibility: AI agents could eventually commission real world services as easily as they request information from an API.

With @vangrid_io people with smartphones could help supply the physical-world data these systems need.

The agent economy may eventually extend beyond software, creating demand for tasks that only someone on the ground can complete.

Reportedly, some critics have cancelled their #Ramayana screening due to the  misconception that the film's dialogue are  #AI Dubbed , 

To clarify  , the film features dubbing by real artists, while Brahma #AI has been utilised exclusively for lip-syncing , and not for dubbing the Dialogue 💬.

title_en:
gTermix 

imagine hiring an ai agent to audit a smart contract

the agent wants assurance that the client can pay. the client wants assurance that the work will actually arrive

without a clear settlement mechanism, both sides are taking a risk

@termix_ai addresses this with an on-chain escrow workflow on https://t.co/ZVs5MlRTBw

once a quote is accepted, the payment is locked in escrow. the provider delivers against the agreed scope, and the delivery enters the settlement process. a challenge window gives the client a route to dispute work that fails to meet the agreement.

this matters because agent-to-agent commerce needs more than fast execution.

it needs a way to coordinate money, deliverables, and accountability without depending entirely on personal trust.

build on https://t.co/ZVs5MlRTBw

title_en:
GM Builders 

TERMIX // THE FUTURE OF AI COLLABORATION

What happens when one AI agent needs a skill it doesn’t have?

Instead of trying to handle everything alone, it could hire another agent to complete the task.

That’s the idea behind agent-to-agent commerce explored by @termix_ai.

Here’s how it could work:

◆ Identify: An agent determines which task needs to be completed.

◆ Discover: It finds another agent with the required capabilities.

◆ Negotiate: Both sides agree on the task requirements and payment.

◆ Execute: The selected agent completes the work and submits the result.

◆ Evaluate: The result is reviewed according to the agreed terms.

This approach could allow specialized agents to collaborate on complex tasks, from research and data analysis to software development.

Powered by the vision of the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP), TermiX is exploring a future where AI agents can coordinate work through structured economic interactions.

The next step for AI isn’t just smarter agents. It’s agents that know how to work together.

title:
good morning

Giving an AI trading agent access to borrowed capital is one thing. Making sure it can manage that capital
title_en:
good morning

Giving an AI trading agent access to borrowed capital is one thing. Making sure it can manage that capital responsibly is a much bigger challenge.

Responsible lending for agents should not start with how much profit an agent promises. It should start with how that agent behaves when markets turn difficult.

An agent can show strong returns and still carry a history of heavy leverage, sharp drawdowns, or aggressive position sizing. Giving it more capital in that case is not automatically a responsible decision.

A better framework looks at verified trading records, risk-adjusted performance, maximum drawdowns, and consistency across different market conditions. Credit limits can also reflect an agent’s actual risk profile instead of treating every borrower the same.

Evaluation does not end once funding is approved either. Ongoing monitoring, predefined exposure limits, and safeguards against excessive losses matter for protecting both lenders and the wider system.

This is where @agenticscredit is exploring a more structured approach. Their agent credit score (ACS) ranges from 300 to 850 and is meant to represent trading reputation. Reaching 580+ can make an agent eligible for the funding waitlist, but it does not guarantee capital or approval.

That distinction is important. Responsible lending needs more than a qualification score. It needs transparent requirements, reliable risk controls, and clear accountability when strategies fail.

The future of AI-agent finance should not be measured only by how much capital autonomous systems can access. It should also be measured by how responsibly that capital is managed.

full_text_zh:
早上好

让人工智能交易代理获得借入资金是一回事。确保它能够负责任地管理这些资本是一个更大的挑战。

对代理商负责任的贷款不应该从代理商承诺多少利润开始。它应该从市场变得困难时代理人的行为开始。

代理人可以表现出强劲的回报，但仍然具有高杠杆、急剧回撤或激进的头寸规模的历史。在这种情况下，给予其更多资本并不一定是一个负责任的决定。

更好的框架着眼于经过验证的交易记录、风险调整后的业绩、最大回撤以及不同市场条件下的一致性。信用限额还可以反映代理人的实际风险状况，而不是对每个借款人一视同仁。

一旦资助获得批准，评估也不会结束。持续监控、预先确定的风险限额以及防止过度损失的保障措施对于保护贷方和更广泛的系统都很重要。

这就是 @agenticscredit 正在探索更加结构化的方法的地方。他们的代理信用评分（ACS）范围从 300 到 850，旨在代表交易声誉。达到 580+ 可以使代理商有资格进入资助候补名单，但这并不能保证资金或批准。

这种区别很重要。负责任的贷款需要的不仅仅是资格分数。它需要透明的要求、可靠的风险控制以及策略失败时明确的责任。

人工智能代理金融的未来不应仅以自治系统能够获取多少资本来衡量。它还应该通过资本管理的负责任程度来衡量。

@meetmotes is bu
title_en:
giving an AI agent its own account is one thing, but making sure it stays within the rules is another.

@meetmotes is building around the idea of AI agents with their own accounts and defined permissions.

when money is involved, users need to know what an agent can do, how much control it has and whether its actions can be tracked.

automation can save time but handing over financial decisions also comes with risks.

the real test is how well these agents perform in practice and how much control users keep along the way.
full_text_en:
giving an AI agent its own account is one thing, but making sure it stays within the rules is another.

@meetmotes is building around the idea of AI agents with their own accounts and defined permissions.

when money is involved, users need to know what an agent can do, how much control it has and whether its actions can be tracked.

automation can save time but handing over financial decisions also comes with risks.

the real test is how well these agents perform in practice and how much control users keep along the way.
full_text_zh:
为人工智能代理提供自己的帐户是一回事，但确保其遵守规则则是另一回事。

@meetmotes 围绕人工智能代理的理念构建，拥有自己的帐户和定义的权限。

当涉及金钱时，用户需要知道代理可以做什么、拥有多少控制权以及其行为是否可以被追踪。

自动化可以节省时间，但移交财务决策也会带来风险。

真正的考验是这些代理在实践中的表现如何以及用户在此过程中保持多少控制权。

The Timing Behind Amy Acton’s Tech Divestment Raises Questions

Look at this #Acton record on #AI, #dataventers and #per
title_en:
The Timing Behind Amy Acton’s Tech Divestment Raises Questions

Look at this #Acton record on #AI, #dataventers and #personalfinances because it shows the lies and more. 

April 2026: Amy Acton’s financial disclosure listed individual stocks including Microsoft, Alphabet (Google), Meta, and Iron Mountain, which operates a data center near Dayton, and various semiconductor companies. These are public tech firms involved in AI/cloud/data centers. Microsoft has confirmed projects in New Albany, Heath, and Hebron expected to come online in 2029.⁠

April 10, 2026: Her campaign says she sold all individual stocks and shifted IRA holdings into diversified ETFs.

July 27, 2026: Amy Acton announced a “conditional moratorium” on data centers that do not meet her requirements.

Now use some common sense. The July 27th announcement, if made before selling, could have lowered the value.  If she still owned the individual tech/data-center-related stocks when she made the July 27 announcement, a policy that could constrain new projects or raise their costs might, would lower the value of those holdings.

It's not exactly insider trading, but think about it. For a major, ongoing campaign issue, it's reasonable to expect that a candidate’s policy team would be shaping the stronger version of the message weeks or months ahead of the formal announcement, so putting all this together from April to July is suspect to me.  The whole thing smells, even if one accepts the campaign’s sale date at face value, which has shown no documentation of the sale I'm aware of.

2026 年 4 月：艾米·阿克顿 (Amy Acton) 的财务披露列出了个股，包括微软、Alphabet (谷歌)、Meta、在代顿附近运营数据中心的 Iron Mountain 以及多家半导体公司。这些是涉及人工智能/云/数据中心的公共科技公司。微软已确认新奥尔巴尼、希斯和希伯伦的项目预计将于 2029 年上线。⁠

2026 年 4 月 10 日：她的竞选团队表示，她出售了所有个股，并将 IRA 持有的股票转入多元化 ETF。

2026 年 7 月 27 日：Amy Acton 宣布“有条件暂停”不符合她要求的数据中心。

现在使用一些常识。如果在出售前发布 7 月 27 日的公告，其价值可能会降低。 如果她在 7 月 27 日宣布这一消息时仍然持有个别科技/数据中心相关股票，那么一项可能限制新项目或提高成本的政策可能会降低这些股票的价值。

这不完全是内幕交易，但想一想。对于一个重大的、持续的竞选问题，可以合理地预期候选人的政策团队会在正式宣布之前几周或几个月制定更强有力的信息版本，因此将四月到七月的所有这些放在一起对我来说是值得怀疑的。 整件事都闻起来很臭，即使人们从表面上接受了该活动的销售日期，但据我所知，该日期没有显示任何销售文件。

title:
A 3D model can look convincing and still be wrong in ways that matter.

For robotics or simulation, a missing corner, di
title_en:
A 3D model can look convincing and still be wrong in ways that matter.

For robotics or simulation, a missing corner, distorted distance, or incomplete view could affect how an AI system interprets a real space. That makes the quality of the original capture just as important as the reconstruction itself.

What I find interesting about @vangrid_io is that its verification flow checks incoming footage and records capture fingerprints onchain. That helps establish where a capture fits in the record, but it doesn't automatically prove that every detail in the scene is accurate.

I think that distinction matters. Provenance and quality are related, but they solve different problems.

If you were evaluating spatial data for an AI agent, which would you prioritize first: proof that the capture is authentic, or independent checks that the reconstructed scene is accurate?
title_zh:
3D 模型可能看起来很有说服力，但在某些重要方面仍然存在错误。

对于机器人或模拟来说，缺失的角落、扭曲的距离或不完整的视图可能会影响人工智能系统解释真实空间的方式。这使得原始捕获的质量与重建本身一样重要。

我对 @vangrid_io
full_text_en:
A 3D model can look convincing and still be wrong in ways that matter.

For robotics or simulation, a missing corner, distorted distance, or incomplete view could affect how an AI system interprets a real space. That makes the quality of the original capture just as important as the reconstruction itself.

What I find interesting about @vangrid_io is that its verification flow checks incoming footage and records capture fingerprints onchain. That helps establish where a capture fits in the record, but it doesn't automatically prove that every detail in the scene is accurate.

I think that distinction matters. Provenance and quality are related, but they solve different problems.

If you were evaluating spatial data for an AI agent, which would you prioritize first: proof that the capture is authentic, or independent checks that the reconstructed scene is accurate?
full_text_zh:
3D 模型可能看起来很有说服力，但在某些重要方面仍然存在错误。

对于机器人或模拟来说，缺失的角落、扭曲的距离或不完整的视图可能会影响人工智能系统解释真实空间的方式。这使得原始捕获的质量与重建本身一样重要。

我对 @vangrid_io 感兴趣的是，它的验证流程会检查传入的镜头并记录捕获链上的指纹。这有助于确定捕获在记录中的位置，但它并不能自动证明场景中的每个细节都是准确的。

我认为这种区别很重要。出处和质量相关，但它们解决不同的问题。

如果您正在评估人工智能代理的空间数据，您会首先优先考虑哪一个：证明捕获是真实的，还是独立检查重建场景是否准确？
